title: Wrap-up and Cleanup
html:
Goal: look back on every step and every sign-off you made on the Agent-DLC flywheel, and clean up the lab resources your team created, in the console and in dependency order, so that the organiser can tear the environment down cleanly after the event, with nothing left billing or orphaned in AWS.

Prerequisites

  • Any of the earlier chapters completed. Resources from chapters you skipped do not exist; skip those rows below.
  • Cleanup is done by admin in console V3 (ConsoleUrl/v3): it involves no separation of duties, and admin holds every permission, so one window is enough.
  • Finish section 2 before the event ends, in order. The environment itself (EC2, CloudFront, the shared infrastructure) is torn down by the organiser after the event (section 3); you neither need nor are able to do anything on the AWS side.

Delete only what your team created in this workshop, and check every name before deleting (the names of everything this workshop creates start with lab or unicorn; the practice account starts with trainee-). Do not delete the platform's shared resources, such as the gateways launchpad-gw, launchpad-kb-gw and launchpad-exp-gw.

1. Recap: one full turn of the flywheel

flowchart LR
  D[Define<br/>criteria table · golden set] --> B[Build<br/>agents · knowledge base]
  B --> E[Evaluate<br/>gate report · judge calibration]
  E --> R[Release<br/>candidate → live · waiver · rollback]
  R --> O[Observe<br/>observability · scorecard · drift watch]
  O --> F[Improve<br/>admission → regression split → next criteria version]
  F --> D
Phase What you did Who signed
Setup (the Setup and Roles chapters) Signed in to console V3, approved a new account, checked the gated release policy gated the organiser preset admin
Define (the Define chapter) Designed the five-dimension criteria table (with a red line) for Unicorn Company's customer service, created three custom LLM judges, reviewed the golden-set source file developer drafted, biz-owner confirmed the expected answers
Build (the Build chapter) Deployed lab-service-assistant (Strands ZIP) and lab-policy-advisor (managed Harness), attached the policy knowledge base lab-unicorn-policies developer
Evaluate (the Evaluate chapter) Entered and published the criteria table unicorn-service-criteria, created the golden set unicorn-service-golden and curated its dev, regression and holdout splits (holdout sealed); ran the release-gate evaluation and saw the verdict order (red lines, denominator, per-dimension thresholds); developer and sme labelled to calibrate the LLM judge developer drafted and published, biz-owner signed the criteria, curated the splits and decided the calibration
Release (the Release chapter) A new version landed on candidate and moved to live after PASS; a waiver, a rollback drill, calls through the public API (/v1/...), Cedar policy at the Gateway, A/B experiment and canary release-ops signed the release and approved the waiver
Observe (the Observe chapter) Observability dashboards and traces, the Standards scorecard, drift watch and decision history —
Improve (the Improve chapter) Thumbs-down and expert feedback entered the admission queue; samples with a human expected answer joined the regression split and drove the next criteria version biz-owner admitted, developer drafted the new version

Throughout, nobody both wrote and approved the standard, and nobody both built and released a version: the server enforced that by username.

2. Clean up the lab resources (console V3, admin)

Order matters: first the experiments that hold shared resources, then the agents, and finally the knowledge base and evaluation resources the agents depended on.

2.1 A/B experiments and canaries

Experiments and canaries create dedicated gateways, A/B tests, online evaluators and temporary targets, and hold the shared experiment gateway. Left alone, they make the next experiment fail outright and stay around indefinitely.

  1. Open Modules → Agent evaluation → A/B experiments (/v3/experiments) in the left navigation. On the Configuration experiments tab on the right of the page header, click each experiment from the Release chapter, click CLEANUP in its CLEANUP card, and confirm in the Clean up experiment dialog.
  2. Switch to the Runtime canaries tab, click each canary, click CLEAN UP, and confirm in the Clean up the canary dialog.

An experiment or canary whose Status in the list already reads Cleaned up (cleaned at the end of the Release chapter) needs nothing more; open it only to check the result.

Expected result: every experiment and canary reads Cleaned up, and its cleanup card lists a per-item result (deleted / skipped). In this run the experiment EXP-lab-service-assistan… lists five items, abtest:, online-eval:, two bundle: and gateway-target:, all deleted. The shared experiment gateway launchpad-exp-gw is kept, by design.

2.2 Online evaluation, reviewer links, drift watch, alerts and API keys

  1. Modules → Agent evaluation → Online evaluation (/v3/online): the online evaluation created in section 6 of Phase 6 · Improve is listed under a configuration name starting with oe_lab_service_assistant_ (its Agent column reads lab-service-assistant; the task description unicorn-service-online you typed is not shown in the list). Click the Delete icon button on that row and click Delete in the Delete online evaluation dialog. Expected result: the list reads "No online evaluation yet". The dialog notes that the results log group /aws/bedrock-agentcore/evaluations/results/oe_lab_service_assistant_… is kept; the organiser handles it.
  2. Reviewer links: Modules → Agent runtime → Issue box (/v3/issues), switch to the Reviewers tab on the right of the page header, and pick lab-service-assistant in the agent drop-down at the top left (it defaults to lab-canary-sandbox, first by name). In the Reviewer links table click Revoke on after-sales policy expert sme from the Improve chapter (and on any other Active link), and click Revoke in the "Revoke this link?" dialog each time. Expected result: those rows read Revoked and their Revoke buttons are greyed out. The reviewer loses access at once; their earlier verdicts are kept.
  3. If you want to keep the environment and only stop spending: in Standards → Drift watch, untick Enabled in the Schedule card and click Save, so the scheduled evaluations stop. Skip this if you are deleting the agents: once the agent is deleted, the schedule is skipped when it falls due and runs no evaluation.
  4. Alert rules: Modules → Agent runtime → Spend & alerts (/v3/costs), switch to Alerts on the right of the page header, click the Delete icon button on the lab-p95-30s card from the Observe chapter and click Delete in the "Delete this rule?" dialog (to only disable it, click the bell icon Enable or disable next to it). Expected result: the tab reads "No rules yet."
  5. API keys: click Agents at the top of the left navigation, open lab-service-assistant, switch to the Access & integration tab, and in the API keys card click Disable on lab-service-assistant-1 (issued in the Release chapter); confirm with Disable in the Disable this key? dialog. Expected result: the row shows Disabled and the button turns into Enable. Clients using it get 401 auth.invalid_api_key at once; the console can only disable keys, not delete them, and the key records go away with the instance.

2.3 Governance policies

Open Modules → Agent runtime → Governance (/v3/governance) and find the launchpad-gw row on the Gateways tab. It ends in two buttons: Policies opens the gateway detail page at its Policies section, Open opens the same page at Overview (section 5.2 of the Release chapter uses Open; both lead to the same page, a V2 page opened inside V3, /v2/governance?view=gateway&...). Work in the reverse order of the Release chapter:

  1. Click Open; in Overview, under Switch Gateway mode, set Target Gateway mode to LOG_ONLY (the Type the Gateway name box disappears once it is selected: rolling back to LOG_ONLY needs no name confirmation, only switching to ENFORCE does), click Apply Gateway mode and click Confirm in the Roll back to LOG_ONLY dialog. Expected result: the gateway update takes a dozen seconds or so; after a page refresh Current Gateway mode reads LOG_ONLY (about 20 seconds and 8 seconds in two runs). An ACTIVE policy cannot be deleted while the gateway enforces (its Delete button is disabled, with the hint "Roll this ACTIVE Policy back to LOG_ONLY (or move the Gateway to LOG_ONLY) before deleting it"), so this comes first.
  2. Switch to the Policies (2) section and click Delete on the unicorn_tool_allowlist and unicorn_payout_admin_only rows, clicking Confirm in the Delete policy dialog each time. Expected result: the section title reads Policies (0) and the table says "No policies on this engine".
  3. The policy engine itself has no delete button on this page; the organiser handles it when tearing down the environment.

Do not delete the shared gateways launchpad-gw and launchpad-kb-gw by hand; they are the platform's shared infrastructure and the organiser handles them when tearing down the environment.

2.4 Delete the agents

Click Agents (/v3/agents) in the pinned entries at the top of the left navigation. For lab-service-assistant, lab-policy-advisor and, only if you did the matching optional steps, lab-legacy-container (the container agent of option A in section 3 of the Build chapter), lab-legacy-agent (the BYOC agent of option B) and lab-canary-sandbox (the canary sandbox agent from section 7 of the Release chapter; finish the canary clean-up in 2.1 first), one by one: click the agent's name in its row to open the agent page, click More → Delete on the right of the page header, type the agent's name (for example lab-service-assistant) into the Type … to confirm box of the "Delete this agent?" dialog ("Delete … and its AgentCore resources. This cannot be undone."), then click Delete. For lab-service-assistant, with its live / candidate endpoints, the two named endpoints are deleted first, so the dialog stays busy for up to about a minute; do not close the page or click again meanwhile. Deleting also removes the Runtime / Harness resources on the AgentCore side.

Named endpoints delete asynchronously. For an agent moved onto live / candidate endpoints, both named endpoints must be deleted before AgentCore allows the Runtime or Harness to be deleted, and a Harness endpoint sits in a deleting state for a minute or two. The console waits for the endpoints for about 45 seconds at most: if they are not gone by then, the agent still disappears from the list, and the backend retries in the background every minute until AWS has let go. So the organiser has to wait for those retries to finish before tearing the environment down; otherwise the backend doing the retries is gone and the Runtime / Harness is left orphaned. Once the agents are deleted, tell the organiser as in section 3.

Expected result: the agents are gone from the Agents list. The Runtime / Harness on the AWS side is usually gone within a few minutes: in this run lab-service-assistant, with its live / candidate endpoints, took under a minute from confirming the deletion until its Runtime and all three endpoints were gone in AWS; the managed Harness lab-policy-advisor took about 2 minutes (the Harness and its DEFAULT endpoint go into a deleting state first); lab-legacy-agent and lab-canary-sandbox each took under 30 seconds. All four agents were gone within 4 minutes. The console does not show that background work, and the organiser checks it in the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore console before tearing down.

2.5 Knowledge base, registry records, evaluators and datasets

  1. Modules → Agent development → Knowledge Bases (/v3/knowledge): open lab-unicorn-policies, click Delete, and click Delete in the Delete knowledge base dialog. Its data sources and gateway target go with it. Expected result: the page returns to the knowledge base list and lab-unicorn-policies disappears from it at once, its gateway target with it; AWS takes about 10 minutes to delete the knowledge base itself (it shows DELETING in the Amazon Bedrock knowledge base list meanwhile), which does not hold up the next steps. If Knowledge base in use appears, an agent still has it attached; do not click DELETE ANYWAY — go back to 2.4.
  2. Modules → Agent development → Registry (/v3/registry): open the records whose names start with lab- (in this run only the skill lab-unicorn-service-rules from the Build chapter; the agents' records went with the agents in 2.4), click Delete, and click Delete in "Delete this record?". Expected result: no record starting with lab- is left; if your team's records were the only ones in the workspace, the registry reads "Nothing registered in this workspace yet". Do not clean up with Disable: disabling is terminal, and the record can then be neither restored nor edited. (The organiser's teardown script deletes every record along with the registry, but delete your team's records here anyway so the console stays clean.)
  3. Modules → Agent evaluation → Evaluators (/v3/evaluators): click the Delete icon button on the row of each custom evaluator from the Define and Evaluate chapters and click Delete in the Delete evaluator dialog (in this run unicorn_fee_check, unicorn_no_overpromise and unicorn_privacy_guard). Expected result: the Custom count in the header reads 0, and AWS deletes them at once. The organiser's teardown script does not remove them, so be sure to delete them here.
  4. Modules → Agent evaluation → Data center (/v3/data): switch to the Datasets tab. The golden set shows up there as four rows: unicorn-service-golden and its three splits unicorn-service-golden·dev, unicorn-service-golden·regression and unicorn-service-golden·holdout. They are managed on the golden set page and cannot be deleted here: Delete answers "A golden set cannot be edited or deleted as a plain dataset." Leave them: they live only in the console database, cost nothing on AWS and disappear with the instance. A plain dataset you imported yourself can be deleted with the Delete icon button on its row and Delete in the Delete dataset dialog.

Criteria tables, golden sets, annotation tasks, release records, waivers and the audit trail live only in the console's database, hold no AWS resources, and disappear with the instance; nothing to do for them.

2.6 The trainee account (optional)

Modules → Configuration → User Management (/v3/users): click the Delete icon button on the row of trainee-<yourname> from the Roles chapter (or open the account and click Delete in its header), and click Delete in the Delete account dialog; the account loses console access at once. It would expire on its own seven days after approval anyway.

3. The environment itself is torn down by the organiser

Your team's EC2 instance, CloudFront distribution and Launchpad's shared infrastructure (the CDK stack launchpad-base, the gateways, Memory, Registry and the rest) live in the organiser's AWS account, and the organiser tears them down after the event, following the "Tear down after the event" section of the Organizer deployment guide. Participants have no AWS access and do nothing on the AWS side.

When section 2 is done, the host tells the organiser "our console cleanup is done", with roughly when the last agent was deleted: the organiser has to let the backend finish deleting those agents' AgentCore resources in the background before tearing the environment down.

4. Where the cost comes from

Source Notes
EC2 instance and CloudFront Billed while the organiser's stack exists; stops when the organiser deletes it
Bedrock model invocations Chat, evaluation replays, LLM judges, A/B traffic and canary traffic all invoke models
AgentCore Runtime / Harness, Memory, Gateway and Evaluations are billed by usage
Knowledge base Vector storage, embeddings and retrieval
CloudWatch Logs, span ingestion and Logs Insights queries

All of this is billed to the AWS account the organiser prepared for your team. The costs shown on the observability pages and in gate reports are estimates (token usage times a price table), meant for comparison and decisions, not a bill. AWS Billing in the organiser's account is the source of truth.

5. Next steps

  • Put your own agent on the flywheel: the team lab in the Team lab chapter offers more retail, e-commerce and OTA scenarios. For your own business you only rewrite the criteria table, the golden set and the policy documents; the rest of the flow stays the same.
  • Bring separation of duties to your team: following the Roles chapter, grant criteria.sign, golden.admit and judge.calibrate to your real business owners, give release operators the operator role, and set the workspace release policy to gated.
  • Keep the flywheel turning: treat production thumbs-down and expert feedback as the source of new samples, recalibrate judges regularly, and let every criteria version sit closer to real users than the last.
  • Go deeper: docs/architecture.md (the Agent-DLC section) and docs/agent-dlc-design.md in the Launchpad source repository are the authoritative description of the features and their design.

Checklist

  • You can say what each of the six flywheel phases did, and who signed
  • Every experiment and canary is cleaned up, the online evaluation configuration and the alert rule are deleted, the reviewer link is revoked, API keys are disabled
  • Gateway launchpad-gw is back on LOG_ONLY and both Cedar policies are deleted
  • Every lab- agent is deleted and gone from the Agents list
  • Knowledge base lab-unicorn-policies, the lab- registry records and the custom evaluators are deleted (the golden set and its splits stay)
  • You have told the organiser that your team's console cleanup is done

Troubleshooting

Symptom Cause Fix
After an agent is deleted, the organiser still sees its Harness in the AgentCore console, deleting The named endpoints are still being deleted asynchronously Keep the environment running and wait a few minutes; the backend retries every minute
Deleting the knowledge base shows Knowledge base in use An agent still has it attached Delete the agent first (2.4), or detach it in the agent and republish
The experiment's cleanup button is unavailable An action of the experiment is still running Wait for it to finish, then clean up
The Delete button of a policy cannot be clicked The Gateway is still in ENFORCE, and an ACTIVE policy cannot be deleted Switch the Gateway back to LOG_ONLY first, as in step 1 of 2.3
